source_text: Quae si quis consideret et examinet, tractatu longo atque argumentis opus non est. Probatio est ad fidem facilis compendio veritatis. Loquitur Dominus ad Petrum: Ego tibi dico, inquit, quia tu es Petrus, et super hanc petram aedificabo Ecclesiam meam, et portae inferorum non vincent eam. Et tibi dabo claves regni coelorum: et quae ligaveris super terram, erunt ligata et in coelis; et quaecumque solveris super terram, erunt soluta et in coelis. Et iterum eidem post resurrectionem suam dicit: Pasce oves meas. Super illum unum aedificat Ecclesiam suam, et illi pascendas mandat oves suas. Et quamvis Apostolis omnibus post resurrectionem suam parem potestatem tribuat et dicat, Sicut misit me Pater, et ego mitto vos: accipite Spiritum sanctum; si cujus remiseritis peccata, remittentur illi, si cujus tenueritis, tenebuntur, tamen, ut unitatem manifestaret, unam cathedram constituit, unitatis ejusdem originem ab uno incipientem sua auctoritate disposuit. Hoc erant utique et caeteri Apostoli quod fuit Petrus, pari consortio praediti et honoris et potestatis, sed exordium ab unitate proficiscitur, et primatus Petro datur, ut una Christi Ecclesia et cathedra una monstretur. Et pastores sunt omnes, et grex unus ostenditur, qui ab Apostolis omnibus unanimi consensione pascatur, ut Ecclesia Christi una monstretur. Quam unam Ecclesiam etiam in Cantico canticorum Spiritus sanctus ex persona Domini designat et dicit: Una est columba mea, perfecta mea, una est matri suae, electa genitrici suae. Hanc Ecclesiae unitiatem qui non tenet, tenere se fidem credit? Qui Ecclesiae renititur et resistit, qui cathedram Petri, super quem fundata est Ecclesia, deserit, in Ecclesia se esse confidit? quando et beatus apostolus Paulus hoc idem doceat et sacramentum unitatis ostendat dicens: Unum corpus et unus spiritus, una spes vocationis vestrae, unus Dominus, una fides, unum Baptisma, unus Deus.
pass_a_gloss: If someone considers and examines this, a long discussion and arguments are not necessary. The proof is easy for faith by means of a summary of the truth. The Lord speaks to Peter, saying: I say to you, that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my Church, and the gates of the underworld will not conquer it. And I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven: and whatever you bind on earth will be bound also in heaven; and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed also in heaven. And again he says to him after his resurrection: Feed my sheep. He builds his Church on him alone, and commands him to feed his sheep. And although he gives equal power to all the Apostles after his resurrection and says, As the Father has sent me, I also send you: receive the Holy Spirit; if you remit the sins of anyone, they will be remitted to them, if you retain those of anyone, they will be retained, nevertheless, in order to show unity, he establishes one chair, and with his authority he arranges the origin of this unity to begin from one. Certainly the other Apostles were the same as Peter, endowed with equal partnership and honor and power, but the beginning proceeds from unity, and primacy is given to Peter, so that one Church of Christ and one chair may be shown. And all are shepherds, and one flock is shown, which is fed by all the Apostles with unanimous consent, so that one Church of Christ may be shown. The Holy Spirit also designates this one Church in the Song of Songs, speaking in the person of the Lord and saying: My dove, my perfect one, is one, she is one to her mother, chosen by her parent. Whoever does not hold this unity of the Church, does he think he holds the faith? Whoever resists and opposes the Church, and deserts the chair of Peter on which the Church is founded, does he trust that he is in the Church? When even the blessed Apostle Paul teaches this same thing and shows the sacrament of unity, saying: One body and one spirit, one hope of your calling, one Lord, one faith, one Baptism, one God.

pass_b_english: If someone considers and examines this matter, a lengthy discussion and detailed arguments are not necessary. The proof for faith is easy, provided through a summary of the truth. The Lord speaks to Peter: "I say to you, you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my Church, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it. And I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven: whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven" (Matt 16:18-19). Again, after his resurrection, he says to him: "Feed my sheep" (John 21:17). He builds his Church on him alone, and commands him to feed his sheep. Although he grants equal power to all the Apostles after his resurrection and says, "As the Father has sent me, I also send you: receive the Holy Spirit. If you forgive the sins of any, they are forgiven them; if you retain the sins of any, they are retained" (John 20:21-23), nevertheless, in order to manifest unity, he establishes one chair, and by his authority he arranges that the origin of this unity proceeds from one. Certainly the other Apostles were exactly what Peter was, endowed with an equal partnership of both honor and power, but the beginning proceeds from unity, and primacy is given to Peter so that one Church of Christ and one chair may be shown. All are shepherds, and one flock is shown, which is fed by all the Apostles with unanimous consent, so that the one Church of Christ may be shown. The Holy Spirit also designates this one Church in the Song of Songs, speaking in the person of the Lord and saying: "My dove, my perfect one, is one; she is the only one of her mother, chosen by her who bore her" (Song 6:9). Whoever does not hold this unity of the Church, does he think he holds the faith? Whoever resists and opposes the Church, and deserts the chair of Peter on which the Church is founded, does he trust that he is in the Church? Especially when the blessed Apostle Paul teaches this same thing and shows the sacrament of unity, saying: "There is one body and one Spirit, one hope of your calling, one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God" (Eph 4:4-6).
